summary: Access request for Model Inspector stuck in pending due to Okta email alias normalization
description:
Issue summary: Several employees and one external contractor report that requests to access the internal Model Inspector tool remain in the support portal 'Pending approval' state indefinitely. Impact: Users cannot access Model Inspector UX, blocking triage of model alerts and slowing oncall work for the ML infra team. Affected users are primarily in us-east and include contractor accounts.

Observed behavior: After submitting an access request, the portal shows 'Pending' and does not progress to an approval step. No approver notifications are sent. The support portal logs show lookup failures when resolving the approver queue key.

Expected behavior: Requests should route to the appropriate approver group and trigger approval notifications.

Environment: production (support-portal + identity-proxy + Okta SCIM).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Sign in as a Redwood employee whose Okta profile uses a plus-addressing alias (e.g., 'alice+infra@redwood.com')
2) Open Support Portal -> Request access -> Choose 'Model Inspector' -> Submit request with reason
3) Observe request status in UI remains 'Pending' for >30m with no approver notification
4) Check support-portal logs and identity-proxy logs for request correlation id
logs: 2026-03-10T15:04:23Z support-portal INFO createRequest request_id=REQ-202603-137351 user="alice+infra@redwood.com" status=pending
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM mapping from Okta to internal identity store normalizes/strips plus-addressing, causing the support portal to compare different email keys (requester vs approver queue key).

Reproduced locally: creating a test SCIM profile with alias 'bob+infra@redwood.com' shows mapping to 'bob@redwood.com' in identity-store, while the request payload contains the original email (plus alias) as source of truth, leading to lookup mismatch.
Confirmed support-portal uses user.email (raw from browser session) to build queue lookup key; approver groups were indexed with normalized emails (identity-store primaryEmail).
Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123456) contains affected users' screenshots.
Correlation observed with recent Okta attribute mapping change rolled out 2026-03-03 (PR referenced below).
comments: 2026-03-10 15:20 Priya Shah: Triaging — multiple reports from ML-infra oncall. Started correlation with identity mappings. Assigned to Liam.
2026-03-10 16:05 Liam O'Connor: Reproduced with test user. identity-store shows normalized email while browser session email retains plus sign. Adding investigation notes and logs.

2026-03-11 09:40 SRE Pager: Noted that approver notification service did not receive payloads because queue lookup returned empty; this is upstream of notifications (so notifications not the root cause).

2026-03-11 11:12 Alice M. (reporter): Confirmed workaround (submit request using corporate email without alias) allowed one user to progress to approval; however many contractor identities cannot switch alias format.

2026-03-12 14:30 Liam O'Connor: Temporary mitigation applied — support-portal now attempts a secondary lookup using normalized email if raw lookup fails (hotfix deployed to prod-us-east). Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-13 10:05 Priya Shah: Requesting follow-up: backfill pending requests and add automated test for alias-preserving flow in CI.
resolution: Mitigation: deployed a hotfix that attempts secondary approver lookup using the identity-store primaryEmail when raw request email lookup fails. Workaround: advise users with plus-addressing to submit requests using the normalized corporate email. Next steps: update SCIM mapping to include 'aliases' as part of identity-store index, backfill ~42 pending requests in the queue, and add unit/integration tests to cover alias normalization. Permanent fix PR planned to change approver-keying to use stable internal id rather than email (tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/support-portal/pull/3012).

Action: Implement long-term change to use internal user ID for queue lookups — owner: Platform — PR open
